chunks: I and Kāmil al-Tammār entered upon Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام). Kāmil said to him, “May I be sacrificed for you, there is a hadith narrated by so-and-so.” He said, “Mention it.” He said, “It was narrated to me that the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وآله) spoke to ʿAlī (عليه السلام) of a thousand gates on the day the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) passed away; each gate opens a thousand gates, so that is a thousand thousand gates.”

He said, “That indeed was so.” I said, “May I be sacrificed for you, has that become manifest to your Shiʿah and your loyal followers?” He said, “O Kāmil, one gate or two gates.” So I said to him, “May I be sacrificed for you, then from a thousand thousand gates of your merit, only one gate or two gates are narrated?”
He said: Then he said, “And what could you possibly narrate of our merit? What you narrate of our merit is nothing but a thousand not joined together.”

key_terms.أَلْفُ أَلْفِ بَابٍ: a thousand thousand gates, i.e. an immense multitude of branches of knowledge
key_terms.بِأَلْفِ بَابٍ: with a thousand gates, meaning major divisions or openings of knowledge
key_terms.شِيعَتِكُمْ: your Shiʿah, the followers devoted to the Imams عليهم السلام
key_terms.غَيْرَ مَعْطُوفَةٍ: not joined together, meaning disconnected or not comprehensively linked
key_terms.فَضْلِكُمْ: your merit or excellence, referring to the virtues of the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام
key_terms.يَفْتَحُ أَلْفَ بَابٍ: opens a thousand gates, indicating expansive branching knowledge

ai.seo_question: How much of the knowledge and merits of the Ahl al-Bayt have been transmitted to people?
ai.summary: This hadith speaks of the vast body of knowledge imparted by the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم to Amīr al-Muʾminīn ʿAlī عليه السلام at the end of the Prophet’s life. It emphasizes that only a very small portion of the merits and knowledge of the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام has reached the Shiʿah. The narration highlights the immensity of their divinely granted knowledge and virtue.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Muhammad, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, fom Muhammad Bin Al Waleed Shaban Al Sayrafi, from Yunus Bin Rabat who said, 
‘I and Kamil Al-Tammar went over to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>. So Kamil said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! There is a Hadeeth which so and so reported’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Mention it’. So he said, ‘It was narrated to me that the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> narrated to Ali<sup>asws</sup> with a thousand topics on the day Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> passed away, each topic opening a thousand topics. So that would be a thousand thousand (a million) topics’.

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It had been that’. I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! So, has that been manifested to your<sup>asws</sup> Shias and your<sup>asws</sup> friends?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Kamil! (Maybe) a topic or two topics’.  So I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! So it has not been reported from your<sup>asws</sup> merits from a thousand thousand (a million) topics except for a topic or two topics?’
He (the narrator) said, ‘So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And perhaps your reports from our<sup>asws</sup> merits, you have not reported from our merits except for a thousand without being read together’.
en.sarwar: 9. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn al-Walid, Shabab al-Sayrafi fromYunus ibn Ribat who has said that once he and Kamil al-Tammar went to see abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.). Kamil said to the Imam (a.s.), “‘May Allah take my soul in service for your cause, there is a hadith which so and so son of so and so has narrated.” The Imam (a.s.) said, “Say and read it.” He (Kamil) then said, “He so and so narrated to me that the Holy Prophet narrated a thousand chapter to Ali on the day the Messenger of Allah died. Each of those chapters open a thousand chapter. The total becomes a Million chapter.”

The Imam (a.s.) said, “That is how it happened.” I then said, “‘May Allah take my soul in service for your cause, has this become manifest to your followers and those who love you?” The Imam (a.s.) said, “O Kamil, only one or two chapters may have become so.”

Kamil has said that the Imam (a.s.) then said, “You perhaps may not be able to narrate all our excellence and virtues. You do not narrate from our excellence and virtue but only a scattered thousand.”
